draft.title: Functional groups in medicines
card: A functional group is a small group of atoms in a molecule that mostly decides how the molecule reacts. Molecules with the same functional group react in similar ways.
Hydroxyl
an -OH group on a carbon chain, found in alcohols. It can form hydrogen bonds with water, which can help a medicine dissolve.
Carboxyl
a -COOH group, found in carboxylic acids. It can give away a hydrogen ion, so the molecule can act as an acid.
Amino
an -NH2 group, found in amines. It can accept a hydrogen ion, so the molecule can act as a base.
draft.remember: Spot the functional group in a medicine's structure to predict how it may react.

a.q: A medicine's structure shows a -COOH group. What does this suggest about how the medicine may react?
opts: It may give away a hydrogen ion, acting as an acid
It may accept a hydrogen ion, acting as a base
It may form hydrogen bonds but cannot react as an acid
It may react in the same way as any alcohol
a.why: A -COOH group is a carboxyl group, and it can give away a hydrogen ion. That makes the molecule able to act as an acid. Accepting a hydrogen ion is the job of the amino group, not the carboxyl group.
a.clue: Which group on the card can give away a hydrogen ion?

b.q: Chemist Priya draws a medicine with an -NH2 group and an -OH group. Which prediction fits both groups?
opts: It may act as a base and form hydrogen bonds with water
It may act as an acid and form hydrogen bonds with water
It may act as a base but cannot form hydrogen bonds
It may act as an acid but cannot form hydrogen bonds
b.why: The amino group can accept a hydrogen ion, so the molecule may act as a base. The hydroxyl group can form hydrogen bonds with water. Acting as an acid would need a -COOH group, which this medicine does not show.
b.clue: Match each group to what it can do, then combine the two.

a.best: It may give away a hydrogen ion, acting as an acid

b.best: It may act as a base and form hydrogen bonds with water

problems.detail: The clue asks which group can 'give away a hydrogen ion'. That phrase matches only the correct option, so the clue gives the answer away instead of prompting recall.

The why says acting as an acid 'would need a -COOH group'. This overstates it: other groups, such as phenolic -OH, can also be acidic. The card only says a carboxyl group can act as an acid, not that it is the only acidic group.

check.summary: The card and answers are correct. The clue for (a) gives the answer away, and the why for (b) wrongly implies that only -COOH can make a molecule acidic.
